pr_title: Fix data query on stale chart
pr_body:
##### Summary
When requesting data for a stale chart it used to do all calculations relative to the last collected timestamp for the chart. This was recently changed to do all calculations on the current time (`now_realtime_sec()`) 

This would allow the chart to generate results (albeit "empty") if such a query would be done. 

This PR removes some restrictions to make this work properly, as currently there are cases where the agent will 
return a 

```
Cannot generate output with these parameters on this chart.
```

##### Test Plan
- In a parent - child setup, start both agents
- Do do a query on the parent agent requesting data for a chart of the child : eg. 
  `localhost:19999/host/child/api/v1/data?chart=system.cpu`
- Stop the child, restart the parent and do again
  `localhost:19999/host/child/api/v1/data?chart=system.cpu`
   On the cloud, for this node you will be getting `Error` when viewing the dashboard
- Apply the PR and retry

This will also work if you setup chart obsoletion / clean orphan hosts. If you set it up say to 30 seconds, then you need not restart the parent. You can stop the child node, wait for the host to be deleted and try the query. 

Fixes #13138
Fixes #12314

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Chart not respecting the time selection when data collection stops
issue_context.body: ### Bug description The following two screenshots show what happened when I gracefully stopped the only child streaming to a parent. In both screenshots you can see at the top charts that are unrelated with streaming and below the charts that are related. Instead of keeping everything synchronized to indeed respect the "last 3 minutes" shown on the datetimepicker, the bottom charts started changing the duration they were showing. The second screenshot shows when this process stopped, which is when the charts ended up showing just two points (two seconds). ### Expected behavior The chart values should be moving to the left, showing either empty data points or zero data points on the right side, but certainly respecting the "last 3 minutes" shown. ### Steps to reproduce There may be more easy ways than to just stop a child, but it certainly works there. ### Installation method kickstart.sh ### System info ```shell Just an ubuntu 20.04 VM ``` ### Netdata build info ```shell Version: netdata v1.35.0-13-nightly Configure options: '--build=x86_64-linux-gnu' '--includedir=${prefix}/include' '--mandir=${prefix}/share/man' '--infodir=${prefix}/share/info' '--disable-silent-rules' '--libdir=${prefix}/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu' '--libexecdir=${prefix}/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu' '--disable-maintainer-mode' '--prefix=/usr' '--sysconfdir=/etc' '--localstatedir=/var' '--libdir=/usr/lib' -fdebug-prefix-map=/usr/src/netdata=. -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat -Werror=format-security' 'LDFLAGS=-Wl,-Bsymbolic-functions -Wl,-z,relro' 'CPPFLAGS=-Wdate-time -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2' 'CXXFLAGS=-g -O2 -fdebug-prefix-map=/usr/src/netdata=. -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat -Werror=format-security' Install type: binpkg-deb Binary architecture: x86_64 Packaging distro: Features: dbengine: YES review_comments: A question, not sure: Could this affect health?...

You can test -- the query would return data relative to the last collected timestamp (last entry t) which could be in the past even if the check would be (assumed) to calculate something from `now - X seconds`

It could affect it I think... But maybe in a better way.

In normal operation I'm observing that before_wanted = last_entry_t.

If by chance (e.g. high load on the host) what health requests as before_wanted is > than last_entry_t (especially in 5s updated charts), the extra null value looks like it is considered in the calculation.

In a test alert, that sums a constant chart for the last minute, health seems to get a different value back when before_wanted = last_entry_t than when before_wanted > last_entry_t.

But: When I re-introduced the removed code from this PR, it seems I get errors when before_wanted > last_entry_t... Not sure why, need to dig more...

I don't think it's a blocker for this PR, but something we need I think to look more into.
